content.thinking:
The test timed out (180 s per tool call). The brute_peak function is slow (it calls naive_U for all 4096 pairs, each O(n·nodes)). With n up to 300, naive_U over 4096 pairs is expensive: 4096 × 300 × ... too slow.

Let me limit the brute-force check to small cases (n ≤ 40) and rely on the py-vs-C comparison for larger ones. Let me restructure: run the brute check only when n ≤ 25, and split the test into two parts so each tool call finishes in time.

arguments.command:
cd /app/tmp && python3 - << 'PY'
s=open('t_e2e2.py').read()
s=s.replace("""    # independent optimality
    br = brute_peak(fib, caps, S, ms)
    assert br == pa, ('not optimal', br, pa, req)""",
"""    # independent optimality (only for small instances: brute force is slow)
    if len(fib) <= 25:
        br = brute_peak(fib, caps, S, ms)
        assert br == pa, ('not optimal', br, pa, req)""")
open('t_e2e2.py','w').write(s)
PY
timeout 175 python3 t_e2e2.py 5 2>&1 | tail -6
